title: The Soviet–Afghan War (1979–1989)
key_facts: Soviet intervention to support the Afghan communist government against mujahideen insurgents
Mujahideen backed by the US, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and others as a Cold War proxy
War ended with Soviet withdrawal in 1989; conflict continued into Afghan civil war
causes: Internal instability in Afghanistan and communist government consolidation
Soviet desire to maintain a friendly regime on its southern border
Cold War rivalry and regional power competition
outcome: Soviet withdrawal under the Geneva Accords (1988)
Significant casualties and economic strain contributing to late‑Soviet crisis
Legacy of regional instability and rise of transnational militancy

figures.name: Babrak Karmal
figures.role: Afghan communist leader backed by the USSR

impacts: Contributed to Soviet economic and political strain
Militarization and refugee crises in the region
